findings.description: F001 says plan_contract classifications remain absolute blocks, while F003 relies on an existing medium plan_contract being neutralized by waived_with_reason. That wording can drive an implementation that blocks the completion-path fixture despite the stated non-goal of changing medium handling.
findings.recommendation: Clarify that plan_contract remains an absolute block only against the new streak-gated waived_matrix_pin_high path, while existing medium/low disposition semantics remain unchanged.

findings.description: F001 introduces a configurable streak threshold N, but the plan does not explicitly pin one shared threshold source across convergence_verdict, lock-refusal messaging, and record_disposition validation. A split default would create eligible-looking refusals that the disposition command later rejects, or the reverse.
findings.recommendation: Add acceptance language and at least one non-default-N test proving the verdict, refusal text, CLI disposition path, and record_disposition validator all use the same threshold value.

findings.description: The proposed tests cover unlocked eligibility and fallback refusal strongly, but the no_streak_blocked and critical_blocked user-facing states are only indirectly covered by helper or matrix expectations. The lock refusal surface should be pinned for those states because it is part of the operator journey.
findings.recommendation: Add lock-decision tests proving below-threshold high matrix_pin findings and critical matrix_pin findings do not emit the unlocked disposition template and remain blocking.
